preamble: The change of dental [dʱ] to an unaspirated retroflex [ɖ] is a two-step development in Indo-Aryan. First, the Old Indo-Aryan cluster -rdh- was retroflexed and assimilated to Middle Indo-Aryan -ḍḍh- (Pali and Prakrit aḍḍha 'half' beside the conservative addha). Then, in varieties that lost breathy voice, the result was deaspirated and simplified to ḍ, as in Sinhala and the Dardic languages Kashmiri and Palula. Most of the Indo-Aryan Midland instead kept aspiration and dental place (Hindi ādhā 'half'), so the outcome is regional.

examples.note: Retroflexion from the -rdh- cluster plus the general Sinhala loss of aspiration; related aḍu 'wanting, imperfect'.
Kashmiri, which lacks voiced aspirates, has unaspirated ḍ; adjective oḍᵘ.

sources: Turner, R. L. (1962–1966). A Comparative Dictionary of the Indo-Aryan Languages, entry 644 ardhá 'half'. https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/soas_query.py?qs=ardha&searchhws=yes
